title: A protocol for generation and live-cell imaging analysis of primary cilia reporter cell lines
protocol: Seed hTERT-RPE-1 Flp-In T-REx TTBK2 KO cells in RPE-1 complete medium supplemented with DOX on a CELLVIEW CELL CULTURE SLIDE, PS, 75/25 MM at high density (∼25.000–30.000 cells per well).
Maintain the cells in the incubator for analysis of primary cilia dynamics over 3-4 days.
Wash cells with PBS or FluoroBrite medium on Day 3.
Add imaging medium supplemented with 1 μg/mL DOX to promote ciliogenesis.
Add approximately 300 μL of imaging medium per well to prevent evaporation during long-term imaging.
Set up an inverted microscope system equipped with an environmental chamber.
Maintain temperature, humidity, and CO2 levels during imaging sessions.
Use a confocal microscope for better signal-to-background noise ratio.
Select water immersion objectives to overcome spherical aberrations in deep specimens.
Choose Zeiss Immersol Immersion oil W 2010 for water oil immersion.
Set up multi-position acquisition using the microscope operating software.
Add specific positions of cells with cilia for imaging.
Equip a laser scanning confocal and epifluorescence microscope LSM800 with an environmental chamber for live-cell imaging.
Control temperature, humidity, and CO2 in the environmental chamber.
Use a C-Apochromat 63×/1.20 Korr UV VIS IR water immersion objective.
Combine solid state laser 488 with high-sensitivity GaAsP detector to acquire images.
Control the microscope using ZEN Blue software.
Acquire data in 1024 × 1024 pixel format.
Set pixel time around 1 μs and pixel size 0.10 μm in bidirectional mode.
Apply 2× averaging with 8-bit bit depth for image acquisition.
Take images as Z-stacks with a thickness of 0.6 μm.
Use slice spacing of 0.5 μm for Z-stack imaging.
Acquire images every 10–15 min over up to 16 hours.
Open the ZEN Blue Software.
Turn on the temperature and atmosphere control in the “Incubation” window.
Set incubation conditions at least 20 minutes before starting the microscope setup.
Insert sample into holder for microscope setup.
Allow system to equilibrate for one hour before imaging.
Put a drop of immersion medium on the selected objective.
Insert the slide with cells into the slide holder and close the chamber with the lid.
Turn on the fluorescence in the “Locate” tab.
Find the focus by looking at the specimen through the eyepiece.
Close the shutter once the sample focus is found to avoid bleaching.
Switch to the “Acquisition” tab.
Select “Z-stack”, “Tiles”, and “Time series” options, and enable “Auto Save”.
Add “+LSM Confocal” in the “Imaging Setup” window.
Add one Track in a “Frame” mode for single-channel imaging.
Select the dye (EGFP) and the color code.
Set the scan speed to achieve a pixel speed around 1 μs in the “Acquisition Mode” window.
Choose bidirectional scanning direction to improve imaging speed.
Use 2× averaging to reduce noise and enhance image quality.
In the “Definite Focus” window, click “Find Surface”, if necessary fine-tune the focus on the center of the cell/cilium and click Store Focus.
Choose “Use Focus Surface/Z Values Defined by Tiles Setup” in the “Focus Strategy” window.
Choose “Local (per Region/Position)” in “Focus Surface”.
Check "Adapt Focus Surface/Z values" with "Definite focus", "Update with Multiple Offsets".
Choose "By Definite Focus: Recall Focus" in "Initial Definition of Support Points/Positions/Tile Regions".
Set the desired number of slices and interval between them in the “Z-stack” window.
Set the duration to "As Long as Possible" or specify a precise number of cycles in the “Time Series” window.
Set an interval between individual time points, typically 10 or 15 minutes.
Fill in the file name and saving path in the “AutoSave” window.
Click “Start Experiment” to begin imaging.
Process Z-stack *.czi files for further analysis using Orthogonal maximal projection.

Seed the hTERT-RPE-1 mNeonGreen-IFT74 reporter cell line in RPE-1 complete medium supplemented with DOX (typically 1 μg/mL) on IBidi ibiTreat μ-Slide 8 well chamber slide at high density (∼25,000 cells per well).
Aspirate the medium from the cells grown in μ-Slide 8 well chamber slide.
Wash the cells with PBS or imaging medium to remove remnants of previous media.
Add Imaging medium (supplemented with 1 μg/mL of DOX) to promote ciliogenesis.
Proceed directly to live-cell imaging after 24 hours to monitor transport of IFT trains.
Take images as time series every 200 ms.
Acquire 150 images in total per time series.
Use an Airyscan detector for increased resolution and signal-to-noise ratio.
Consider using spinning disk confocal microscopy for IFT imaging.
Alternatively, use Total Internal Reflection Fluorescent (TIRF) microscopy for IFT imaging.
Use "TIRF-like" microscopy for IFT imaging to reduce bleaching of fluorescence signals.
Employ an oil objective with high numerical aperture (NA) for higher resolution imaging.
Combine the oil objective with Airyscan detector for enhanced imaging quality.
Prepare the microscope according to your needs before beginning imaging.
Open the ZEN Black acquisition software.
Put a drop of the appropriate immersion medium on the selected objective.
Insert the μ-Slide 8 well coverslips with the cells in the slide holder.
Turn on the fluorescence in the “Locate” tab and find the focus with the eyepiece.
Select the “Acquisition” tab and tick “Time Series”.
Set laser line attenuator transmission for the 488 nm wavelength (to 0.5%).
Select “Airyscan Mode / SR” in the “Channels” window.
Set “Cycles” up to 150 and “Intervals” to 200 ms in the “Time Series” window.
Adjust focus on primary cilia while in “Live mode”.
Select a region of interest containing the cilium for analysis.
Click on “Start Experiment”.
Go to the “Processing” window and select “Airyscan Processing”.
Select “Apply” after choosing appropriate settings.
Use Airyscan processing for post-acquisition resolution improvement.
Generate a processed ∗.czi file with enhanced resolution.
Repeat steps 45–47 to obtain a sufficient number of recordings of primary cilia per each condition of your experiment.
Measure at least 20 primary cilia per experimental condition for robust data analysis.
Set the imaging interval to take an image every 200 ms with a total of 150 images.
Minimize laser power to reduce bleaching of IFT trains.
Adjust parameters according to your needs to optimize results.
Start the Fiji software to open an Airyscan processed *.czi file.
Click on Image → Adjust → Brightness/Contrast for adjustment of brightness and contrast.
Right-click on a straight line in the Fiji toolbar and choose Segmented Line.
Draw a segmented line from the base to the tip of the primary cilium.
Select “Analyze” → “Measure” or use keyboard shortcut Ctrl+M to measure the length of the cilium.
The measured length will be displayed as μm in the “Results” window.
Open the “ROI Manager” in Fiji by selecting “Analyze” → “Tools” → “ROI Manager”.
Click on “Analyze” → “Multi Kymograph” → “Multi Kymograph” (with Linewidth 1) to create a kymograph from the time-lapse data.
Rotate the image 90 degrees by left-clicking on “Image” → “Transform” → “Rotate 90 Degrees Left”.
Select the "ROI Manager" panel.
Click "Measure".
Note that only the IFT train trajectories tracked in the kymograph will be measured.
Obtain values representing an angle between each measured trajectory and the horizontal axis.
Calculate the speed of IFT train by multiplying pixel size and frequency (frames per second).
Convert the unit of tan(angle) into μm/s using pixel size and frequency.
Positive angle values represent anterograde transport.
Negative angle values represent retrograde transport.
Draw an additional line to cover all IFT particles recorded in the time-lapse movie if necessary.
Switch on the microscope, camera, and 488 nm laser illumination.
Install the objective-heating collar and environmental control stage insert.
Allow at least 20 min for temperature, CO2 and humidity to stabilize before inserting the sample.
Start the NIS Elements software.
Apply immersion oil to the objective.
Insert a glass bottom dish with the cells.
Switch on the “Perfect Focus” system.
Slowly raise the objective until the immersion oil makes contact with the glass bottom of the dish.
Keep raising the objective until the microscope emits a beep and the “Perfect Focus” button stops flashing.
Set up one microscope configuration with low laser power for sample screening.
Set up another microscope configuration with higher laser power for acquisition.
Set exposure time, illumination angle, and laser power as main parameters.
Optionally set region of interest.
Ensure signal-to-background ratio above 1.5 for reliable tracking of IFT trains.
Start “Live” acquisition in NIS Elements.
Position the sample to have at least one cilium in the field of view.
Select an appropriate exposure time in the “DU-888 Settings” window based on experimental requirements.
Adjust illumination angle for each experiment individually by moving the beam position in X and Y in the “Lapp H-TIRF XY-F Pad” window.
Determine the critical angle for true TIRF illumination.
Reduce the angle step-by-step towards epi-illumination until cilia start to be visible.
Stop when the signal from the ciliary marker is eclipsed by the fluorescence background.
Move to a different field of view and verify that the signal-to-background ratio is optimal.
Use laser power between 50% and 75% for no more than 40 seconds during acquisition.
Set laser power to the lowest level (e.g., 10%) which allows localizing the cilia when screening samples.
Record several experimental movies to determine if there is significant bleaching of fluorophores or cell damage.
Check “ROI” box at the “DU-888 Settings” panel and define the region of interest of 128 × 128 pixels for fast single cilium acquisitions.
Create a button in the OC panel by duplicating an existing TIRF configuration.
Right-click on the button and choose “Assign current microscope settings” to update the configuration.
Change the microscope settings to the desired acquisition configuration.
Create another new button after changing the settings.
Right-click on the new button and choose “Assign current microscope settings”.
Define the experiment flow in the “ND Acquisition” window.
In the “Time” panel, select one phase with interval option “No delay”.
In the “Lambda” panel, select one optical configuration and set it to the high-power illumination configuration.
Check “Phase 1” only in the “Time” panel, set “Interval” to “No Delay”, and set “Duration” to the desired value.
Check the first “Opt. Conf.” option in the “Lambda” panel and set it to the optical configuration prepared for acquisition.
Set the path for saving movies and appropriate filename base.
Switch to the low-power screening configuration and start searching for a suitable cilium to image.
Move the found cilium to the center of the field of view.
Focus on the cilium with the “Perfect Focus” offset control.
If using the region of interest option, switch on the “ROI” in the “Camera panel”.
Reposition the cilium to be fully contained in the visible area.
Press the “Run now” button in the “ND Acquisition” window.
Switch to the high-power illumination configuration for recording the movie.
Organize the microscope workplace and software layout for easy access to necessary knobs and buttons.
Switch back to the low-power screening configuration after recording.
Repeat the process with more cilia.
Review the recorded movie using NIS elements or Fiji to ensure image quality is satisfactory.
